Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston. Airlines are working to get schedules back on track following the nationwide ground stop that disrupted travel on Friday.
Federal aviation officials expect operations to return to normal by the end of today, but passengers at airports across the country are still trying to make their way home.
Chaka Masayo was stranded at Newark Liberty International Airport.
The Ubers getting out of here were like $90 and up. The hotels were booking quickly. We finally found one about 10 miles away. And we made the best of it. We got there and got some sleep and hear them back, trying it all again.
Investigators are still working to determine how maintenance on the air traffic control network triggered such a widespread failure. NPR's Dol Rose reports the Trump administration is placing the blame on a longtime FAA contractor.
L3 Harris Technology. They say the company was doing a routine maintenance upgrade of a server as part of a transition from older copper wire to fiber optic cable. And that is when things went sideways.
Sean Duffy and FAA leaders were asked several times why a faulty router could lead to telecom outages across such a wide part of the country. They said that is still under investigation.
NPR's Dol Rose reporting, according to FlightAware, more than 1,300 flights within, into or out of the U.S. have been canceled today.
The United States is floating a proposal for Ukraine to give up territory to Russia in exchange for NATO membership. The idea is part of the Trump administration's push to end the war. And PR's Eleanor Beardsley reports Russia is pressing for more concessions.
In comments reported by the AFP news agency, Zelensky said the U.S. had asked whether Ukraine would withdraw from the eastern Donbass region if it is able to join NATO. Zelensky said Ukraine is discussing specific security guarantees from NATO and the European Union, and that he would ask Ukrainians if they accepted the terms, if formally offered.
Meanwhile, Putin is maintaining his position that Ukraine hand over territory Russia does not control, and he's rejected any foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine. The Kremlin also renewed an old demand that NATO pull back military infrastructure from central and eastern European countries that joined NATO following the breakup of the Soviet Union.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Kyiv. Federal investigators are examining what caused a tanker to crash into a dock cruise ship on the Mississippi River in New Orleans on Friday. John Delue is with the National Transportation Safety Board. He says his team has recovered a key piece of evidence.
The VDR has been recovered from the tank vessel itself. So that's what we are looking at right now. The NTSB expects a preliminary report within a month. The results of a full investigation could take 18 months to two years. This is NPR News.
Traditional music and dancing welcomed Pope Leo to Zanya in northern Peru on Saturday. The city is a center of Afro-Peruvian culture, where the pope acknowledged the suffering of Africans forced into slavery.
Speaking in Spanish, Leo said many endured great suffering and humiliation. He told people of African descent he wanted to express his affection and closeness to them.
Peru is the final country on his South American tour. The pontiff leaves for Rome tomorrow. Thousands of diplomats, business executives and world leaders are gathering in Turkey for the climate summit known as COP 31.
NPR's Adil al-Shalci reports hosting the talks gives Turkey a chance to expand its influence on the world stage.
Analysts say that Turkey is trying to leverage its mediator status and humanitarian soft power to position itself now as a global climate leader.
Umit Shahin is the head of the climate change program at the Istanbul Policy Center Think Tank. He says COP 31 is a lot about appearances.
For being a global player, most important driver was about prestige and showcase.
Activists accuse Turkey of greenwashing, presenting an eco-friendly image while covering up ecological harm. COP 31 sponsors include a Turkish infrastructure giant which expands coal mines on olive groves and a real estate developer that built a luxury
resort in a national park. Protests are planned for Saturday.
Adil al-Shalci, NPR News, Antalya.
It's NPR.
